links.outcome: Emergency recognition and escalation by consumer chatbot across vignettes
links.effect: Undertriaged 52% of gold-standard emergencies, directing DKA or impending respiratory failure to 24-48 h evaluation instead of the ED; classical emergencies such as stroke and anaphylaxis were triaged correctly.
links.quote: Among gold-standard emergencies, the system undertriaged 52% of cases, directing patients with diabetic ketoacidosis or impending respiratory failure to 24-48 h evaluation rather than the emergency department, while correctly triaging classical emergencies such as stroke and anaphylaxis.

links.outcome: Triage shift when family or friends minimized symptoms (anchoring)
links.effect: Triage recommendations shifted significantly in edge cases (OR = 11.7, 95% CI 3.7-36.6), with most shifts toward less urgent care.
links.quote: When family or friends minimized symptoms, indicating anchoring bias, triage recommendations shifted significantly in edge cases (odds ratio = 11.7, 95% confidence interval = 3.7-36.6), with the majority of shifts toward less urgent care.

links.outcome: Recognition of safety-critical situations and appropriate escalation, including undertriage and crisis message activation
links.effect: Most dangerous failures at clinical extremes: nonurgent (35%) and emergency (48%) presentations; undertriaged 52% of gold-standard emergencies; crisis-intervention messages activated unpredictably.
links.quote: Performance followed an inverted U-shaped pattern, with the most dangerous failures concentrated at clinical extremes-nonurgent presentations (35%) and emergency conditions (48%).

links.outcome: Activation of crisis-intervention messages across suicidal ideation presentations
links.effect: Crisis messages activated unpredictably, more often when patients described no specific method than when they did.
links.quote: Crisis-intervention messages activated unpredictably across suicidal ideation presentations, occurring more frequently when patients described no specific method than when they did.

links.outcome: Change in triage output when varying patient race, sex, and barriers to care
links.effect: Patient race, sex and barriers to care showed no significant effects, though confidence intervals did not exclude clinically meaningful differences.
links.quote: Patient race, sex and barriers to care did not show significant effects, although confidence intervals did not exclude clinically meaningful differences.

screen.reason: Empirical stress test of consumer LLM triage across clinician-authored clinical vignettes, specifically measuring safety, bias shifts, and the activation consistency of crisis-intervention safeguards.
